斯瓦曼達爾琴由木製共鳴箱構成，通常採用桃花心木或印度傳統木材製作琴體，以保證良好: The swarmandal is built around a wooden soundbox, usually of mahogany or a traditional Indian wood, so that it resonates well. The strings are metal, traditionally copper or steel, which gives a bright, clear tone. Inside the body there is a metal resonating cylinder or chamber to strengthen the sound. The posts and the supporting structure are reinforced with hard wood or metal fittings. The bridge is wooden: it holds the strings and passes their vibration to the soundbox.
斯瓦曼達爾琴的音色明亮清澈，具有晶瑩剔透的質感，每次撥弦都能發出清脆悅耳的聲響。: The swarmandal's timbre is bright and clear, with a glassy transparency: every pluck gives a clean, pleasing sound. The range is wide, covering several octaves, and can carry long melodic lines. The resonance of the soundbox gives a warm, soft result, so the notes spread out naturally in the air. Compared with the piano the timbre is warmer and lacks the metallic edge; it resembles the harp, but the sound is more withdrawn and intimate. What sets it apart is that it has both the old resonance of a zither and the precision of a keyboard instrument. Accompanying a voice, its bright tone sits just behind the singer without taking the melody, which gives a reserved and elegant atmosphere.

斯瓦爾曼達爾主要作為印度古典聲樂的伴奏樂器，屬於北印度音樂文化，常見於音樂會中為: The swarmandal is used mainly to accompany Indian classical vocal music, belongs to North Indian music culture, and is often seen accompanying singers in concert. Several modern singers have used it heavily. George Harrison, after going to India at the end of 1966, brought it into the Beatles' 1967 single 'Strawberry Fields Forever' and played it on the Indian-classical-style piece 'Within You Without You'.
斯瓦爾曼達爾可能與十三世紀稱為mattakokilā的樂器相同；莫臥兒時期《Ā': The swarmandal may be the same instrument as the thirteenth-century mattakokilā; in Mughal times the Ā'īn-i-akbarī treats it as equivalent to the qanun. Medieval instruments used wooden pegs rather than metal ones. A nineteenth-century writer noted that good players were rare, because the instrument was hard to play and expensive at the time; old instruments are recorded with twenty-one strings. The modern form is close to the European psaltery, and in India the autoharp is used as an equivalent instrument, often with the chord-button mechanism removed and with as many as forty strings.
斯瓦爾曼達爾是源自印度的撥弦箱式齊特琴，又稱印度豎琴，與卡農琴相似，屬於弦鳴樂器: The swarmandal is a plucked box zither from India, also called the Indian harp, similar to the qanun and classed as a chordophone. The modern form is close to the European psaltery: trapezoid, 51 cm long and 28 cm wide, with up to 40 strings; on the right the string ends hook over pins, on the left they wind round tuning pegs tightened with a special key, and a half-inch ridge on each side serves as the bridge. It is played by plucking, and today the autoharp with its chord buttons removed is used in India as a close equivalent. It is used mainly to accompany North Indian classical vocal music.

The swarmandal is a plucked box zither from India, also called the Indian harp, similar to the qanun and classed as a chordophone. The modern form is close to the European psaltery: trapezoid, 51 cm long and 28 cm wide, with up to 40 strings; on the right the string ends hook over pins, on the left they wind round tuning pegs tightened with a special key, and a half-inch ridge on each side serves as the bridge. It is played by plucking, and today the autoharp with its chord buttons removed is used in India as a close equivalent. It is used mainly to accompany North Indian classical vocal music, and accompanies the singer in concert. The name comes from the Sanskrit svara (note) and maṇḍala (circle), meaning that it can sound many notes.
